messages:
alex: Heads up everyone, seeing an unusual pattern in us-south GPU fleet — ~12 nodes intermittently drop from scheduling and show driver Xid 31 in dmesg. Not full node crash, but jobs get stuck. :rotating_light:
priya: oncall alerted, I'm on it. Which rack/az?
jamie: logs from one host: ```[ 10432.857642] NVRM: Xid (31) at 0x20000000 0x00000000 0x00000000 0x00000000
[ 10432.857644] NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus```. Hostname p-gpu-us-south-az3-17.
chao: thanks — that Xid31 pattern usually points at PCIe transient resets or firmware/driver mismatch. Anything changed in kernel/drivers recently?
alex: We rolled a small kernel bump on that az yesterday (5.15.102 -> 5.15.110) for CPU microcode. Roll was canaryed then ramped. Only us-south az3 hit full.
marta: Customer impact so far: a handful of active Dedicated jobs hit retries, autoscaler moved some batches but latency spiked. Early estimate: ~2% token drop for affected customers.
ben: If it's PCIe link flapping, we should drain affected nodes and pivot traffic. Suggest draining the 12 hosts with `fleetctl drain` then route jobs to eu-west + burst pool. Cost tradeoff: eu-west spot + inter-region egress ~+$0.04/token for affected workloads. We need approval.
lina: tagging security/compliance — any sensitive workloads on those Dedicated nodes?
priya: quick inventory: 3 dedicated clusters (cust-42, cust-88, internal-test). cust-88 has one long-running fine-tune; Customer Success (cc @marta) is being notified.
jamie: repro attempt shows GPU still responsive for nvml queries during the condition, but driver loses link intermittently. Attached kernel logs show repeated pcie link down/up. ```May  3 10:54:12 host kernel: pcieport 0000:3c:00.0: AER: Uncorrected (Non-Fatal) error received: tx_timeout```. 
chao: Plan I'd run: 1) cordon+drain affected nodes 2) mark them for hw RMA (nvme/pcie riser inspection) 3) provision temporary capacity in eu-west and aps1 for critical tenants 4) schedule firmware downgrade/driver rollback on a test host
alex: Agreed. Start drain now. priya, can you run the drain and update scheduler to avoid rescheduling on same AZ?
priya: running `fleetctl cordon p-gpu-us-south-az3-17 && fleetctl drain p-gpu-us-south-az3-17` now. Doing in small batches (2-3 nodes) to limit churn.
priya: update: drained 3 nodes, autoscaler spun up 5 nodes in eu-west and 2 in aps1 for short-term capacity.
marta: Notifying cust-88 rep: "We've shifted some jobs for resilience; you may see a brief slowdown. CSI ticket #CS-2026-137 raised."
ben: FYI finance: traffic shift will cost an estimated $1.2k over next 6 hours if we keep eu-west burst. OK to proceed? (cc @marta)
marta: proceed, prioritize customer SLAs.
jamie: running targeted repro on test host: rolled driver 525.116 -> 525.105 (older vendor driver) and retesting. If link flaps reduce, we'll plan controlled rollback.
chao: also tagging hw: please provision squad to inspect riser connectors in az3 racks tomorrow AM. Hardware ticket #HW-4982.
lin a: (typo) lina: small note: we've got audit-sensitive workloads only in cust-42 which is untouched. Good.
priya: after draining 9 more nodes, scheduling stable. One job hit retry loop; fixed by increasing max_retries for that route.
alex: Can we set a soft-fallback policy to prefer regional fallback (eu-west then aps1) automatically if >5 partial node failures in an AZ? Avoid manual shifts next time.
chao: we have policy config but it's not enabled for this class. I'll open an infra change PR to add a threshold-based fallback route.
priya: last drained node in batch 4 done. Total drained: 12. No new Xid31 reports in non-drained nodes yet.
jamie: driver rollback on test host reduced pcie link errors during 30m soak. Patch diff and testing notes in the incident doc.
priya: closing the fire with current mitigation: drained nodes, burst capacity live, customer notified, hw ticket created. Keeping thread open for postmortem. :white_check_mark:
deploy-bot: Canary rollback job started for driver image james/driver-525.105 at 2026-05-03T12:40:01Z
alex: thanks all. Postmortem owners: jamie + chao + priya. Please include timelines, cost impact, and an action plan (firmware/driver policy + auto-fallback rules).
oncall-bot: Incident updated: INC-2026-2273 set to 'mitigated' by priya at 2026-05-03T13:02:11Z
priya: saving logs to S3: s3://infra-logs/incidents/INC-2026-2273/*
marta: I'll coordinate customer follow-ups tomorrow. Good work team. :thumbsup:
